candidates.name: Central Nervous System Lymphoma
support_spans: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement
Enhancement of several cranial nerves including bilateral vagus nerves
Lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features on light microscopy
Flow cytometry showed κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation
candidates.why: The combination of leptomeningeal enhancement, cranial nerve enhancement, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features and B-cell lymphoma is consistent with Central Nervous System Lymphoma.

candidates.name: Leptomeningeal metastasis
support_spans: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement
Enhancement of several cranial nerves including bilateral vagus nerves
candidates.why: The patient's history of chemotherapy and autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplant increases the risk of leptomeningeal metastasis, which is supported by the imaging studies showing diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement and enhancement of several cranial nerves.

candidates.name: Richter's transformation
support_spans: past medical history included fatigue several years prior, when he received chemotherapy (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, vincristine, and prednisone) followed by autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplant
κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation
candidates.why: The patient's history of chemotherapy and the presence of κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation suggest the possibility of Richter's transformation, which is a transformation of chronic lymphocytic leukemia to a more aggressive lymphoma.
